page: Microsoft Azure E32d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server is equipped with 1229 GB of local SSD storage, while containing no dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place the E32d_v5 in the average tier for most compute tasks, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1900.18 and a multi-core score of 31085.46. However, its memory subsystem demonstrates strong performance, as evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 2756.95, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Large block memory bandwidth reaches 148.27 GB/sec for read-only operations and 68.94 GB/sec for write operations. For specialized workloads, the system achieves a strong text generation speed of 280.92 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM model, though it drops to a weak 6.65 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a large 70B model due to the lack of GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32d_v5 offers a high density of RAM and bundled local SSD storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of GPU-accelerated instances. The presence of 1229 GB of local SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data. This hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
